## 2. Three reusable finite lemmas

### 2.1 Exact name-index algebra and local freshness

**Lemma INDEX.** On indexes reachable from empty by psErasureIndexInsert/Prepend, Find returns the first entry of the corresponding ordered exact-key list. Inserting (k,v) makes lookup of k return v; lookup of a different exact key is unchanged. Prepend(entries,tail) gives entries' original first-entry precedence over tail. Proof: define a valid depth-d index to be empty, or at positive depth a branch of valid depth-(d−1) indexes, or at depth 0 a bucket. Bucket and Set follow the same low-bit route and divide the hash by two at every positive depth. Induct on d. At zero, Set replaces exactly that bucket. At a positive depth, it updates exactly the selected child and retains the other; starting from empty creates the corresponding empty children. Thus retrieving the route just written obtains its new bucket, while every different route keeps its bucket. Insert prepends the exact key to that bucket, and FindInBucket compares full PsName equality in list order. Different keys on the same route are skipped, not confused. Prepend processes the tail first and then inserts the head, so another list induction proves first-entry precedence. The fixed depth is 16; cryptographic collision resistance is irrelevant. [B]

The key premise is exact structural PsName equality, with equal names routed equally. FN compares name constructors recursively, canonical strings by scalar iteration, and numeric components by Nat equality. Its string traversal budget is one plus the left UTF-8 byte size, so under the declared scalar/next-position laws every compared scalar is visited and the terminal position is inspected. Equal names then have equal hash results by substitution into ENV's deterministic hash function. No injectivity of psNameToString is assumed: different internal name shapes can print alike. ### 2.2 Core opening, closing and typed substitution

Let LC_d(e) mean that every bound index occurring under b additional local binders is less than d+b; free variables use the actual external Core frame. LC_0 is local closure. The exact code has eleven expression constructors. Lift changes bvar i at or above its cutoff to i+amount.
